(album)"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" New for 1964 songs included \"I Like It Like That\" (the Top 30 title song), the Bobby Rogers-led flip side \"You're So Fine and Sweet,\"(this is the \"only\" Show that year, and \"Would I Love You\", a song that became a popular regional hit tune for the group in Pennsylvania and The Midwest.","title":"I Like It Like That (album)"},{"sentence_id":4,"text":" The album also featured a Claudette Robinson-led cover version of the Orlons' #2 Pop smash, \"The Wah Watusi\".","title":"I Like It Like That (album)"},{"sentence_id":5,"text":" (Claudette is also featured with the rest of the group on the album's cover), and the group's 1963 Top 40 Hit, \"I Gotta Dance to Keep From Crying\".","title":"I Like It Like That (album)"},{"sentence_id":6,"text":" Several of the group's other 1964 songs, including the chart hits \"(You Can't Let the Boy Overpower) The Man in You\", \"Come On Do the Jerk\", and its \"B\" side, \"Baby Don't You Go\", were not included.","title":"I Like It Like That (album)"},{"sentence_id":7,"text":" The new 1964 recordings \"I Like It Like That\", \"Would I love You\" and \"That's What Love Is Made Of\" were included on the only US Miracles 1964 album release \"Miracles Greatest Hits From The Beginning\" which was the first double album released by Motown Records.","title":"I Like It Like That (album)"},{"sentence_id":0,"text":"\"A Love She Can Count On\" (Tamla 54078) was a 1963 hit single by Motown Records R&B group The Miracles, issued on that label's Tamla subsidiary label.","title":"A Love She Can Count On"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" It was taken from their album \"The Fabulous Miracles\", and was the follow-up to the group's million-selling Grammy Hall of Fame inducted tune, \"You've Really Got A Hold On Me\".","title":"A Love She Can Count On"},{"sentence_id":0,"text":"\"After All\" is a 1960 song written by Smokey Robinson and originally recorded and released by The Miracles on the Tamla label.","title":"After All (The Miracles song)"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" It was later covered as an unreleased single by The Supremes for Tamla; it was canceled in favor of the single \"Buttered Popcorn\", and their cover wasn't released until it appeared on the 2000 box set, \"The Supremes\".","title":"After All (The Miracles song)"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" The song is noted for both groups' unusual choices for leads.","title":"After All (The Miracles song)"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" For the Miracles' version it serves as a rare lead for Claudette Rogers Robinson, instead of the group’s main lead, Claudette's husband, Smokey Robinson.","title":"After All (The Miracles song)"},{"sentence_id":4,"text":" In the Supremes' case it is their only single to feature Barbara Martin singing on lead vocals (although she does have a spoken line during the song \"(He's) Seventeen\").","title":"After All (The Miracles song)"},{"sentence_id":5,"text":" Florence Ballard, Mary Wilson, and Diana Ross sing verses, and Martin sings the bridge (usually Ballard or Ross was given the lead on the group's recordings at that time).","title":"After All (The Miracles song)"},{"sentence_id":6,"text":" \"After All\" was also later covered by The Marvelettes, in the early 1970s, with group member Wanda Young Rogers as lead.","title":"After All (The Miracles song)"},{"sentence_id":7,"text":" (There's a connection to the two previous groups in that Wanda Young was the wife of Miracles member Bobby Rogers, and she was the only member of The Marvelettes on the song—as with the late-1960s singles of The Supremes, The Andantes served as background singers.)","title":"After All (The Miracles song)"},{"sentence_id":8,"text":" Their version appears on the album \"The Return of the Marvelettes\", and later became the group's belated final single (it failed to chart).","title":"After All (The Miracles song)"}],"peer_messages":[],"previous_answer":null,"question":"What is the name of the album on which the Beatles covered a song from the album The Fabulous Miracles by The Miracles?"}
